observations.text: In Ezek.14.7 'consult' carries the nuance of hypocritical or corrupted inquiry -- the idolater comes to a prophet to consult God while harboring idols in his heart; the impact is that the surface act of seeking is emptied of sincerity, contrasting sharply with the sincere seeking of Isa.55.6 and 2Chr.1.5.

Other M-codes in Ezek.14.7 (M01 sojourn, M64 separates, M47 heart, M15 putting, M77 stumbling block, M56 iniquity, M43 prophet, M22 answer) surround the consulting act but are not positively related to it: darash here is corrupted by co-present idolatry (M77/M56) rather than harmonizing with them -- the seeking is nullified by what accompanies it, a distinct vantage from any prior finding.

In Ezek.14.7, H1875 is the role-T3 operation: the idolater ('any one', party) initiates consulting, directed toward God via a prophet (parties), though the act is compromised by the idolater's simultaneous devotion to idols.

Isa.31.1 and Ezek.14.7 both use 'consult' of illegitimate or compromised inquiry -- Isa.31.1 negates true consultation of the Lord in favor of trust in horses/chariots, while Ezek.14.7 depicts an idolater hypocritically approaching a prophet to consult God while harboring idols in his heart. Both instances show darash's consultation-sense corrupted or withheld by competing loyalties.

Seeking takes hold rightly under conditions of wholeheartedness and sincerity: 'set your mind and heart to seek' (1Chr.22.19), 'with all their heart and with all their soul' (2Chr.15.12), and freedom from co-present idolatry -- in Ezek.14.7 the presence of idols in the heart is what disqualifies otherwise-outward consultation. Genuine seeking requires an undivided heart free from rival objects of devotion.

Seeking is blocked or nullified when the heart harbors idols or a stumbling block of iniquity even while outwardly consulting God -- Ezek.14.3, 14.7 explicitly describe men who 'have taken their idols into their hearts' yet 'come to a prophet to consult me' -- God declares he will not let himself be consulted (or will answer in judgment) in such cases; similarly pride (Ps.10.4 'in the pride of his face') suppresses seeking altogether.

The person whose outward act of inquiry does not take hold rightly is inwardly divided: Ezek.14.3-7 describes them as having 'taken their idols into their hearts' and 'put the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face' -- the inner-being state is one of divided loyalty and self-deception, performing the religious gesture of consultation while the heart remains given to a rival object of devotion.

Uptake of a sought answer from another (a prophet, an oracle) is blocked when the inquirer's heart harbors rival loyalties -- Ezek.14.3-7 shows that idols hidden in the heart nullify the legitimacy of the consultation even though the outward act of inquiry is performed; genuine uptake requires the wholehearted disposition seen elsewhere (2Chr.15.12).

The person who inquires but does not genuinely take up what is sought (as in Ezek.14.3-7) is inwardly divided, harboring 'idols... into their heart' and 'the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face' -- an inner-being state of duplicity, where the outward gesture of consultation masks an unyielded heart.

The pattern of engagement shows heart/soul faculties (mind, will, affection) consistently engaged when seeking is genuine (1Chr.22.19 'set your mind and heart', 2Chr.15.12 'with all their heart and with all their soul'), while purely external/ritual engagement without heart involvement is exposed as illegitimate (Ezek.14.3-7) -- indicating the characteristic's nature is fundamentally a volitional-relational act requiring the engagement of the inner faculties, not a mechanical or merely verbal performance.

At its edge, seeking excludes casual, passive, or half-hearted attention -- it resists mere outward performance without inner devotion (Ezek.14.3-7's idol-hearted consulters are the negative exemplar), and it excludes self-sufficiency/pride that renders inquiry unnecessary (Ps.10.4).
